post.caption: This diamond was cut for candlelight. The old mine cut was common from the 1700s into the late 1800s, and GIA says the cut was designed to sparkle in candlelight. Its soft, squarish outline resembles a modern cushion cut, the table is small and the crown is high, and the large flat culet can be seen through the table. The old European cut is round and was popular from 1890 to 1930. Each one is hand cut, so collectors prize their character. They flash bold colored fire, with less brilliance than modern cuts. GIA gives no cut grade to old European cut diamonds.
